name: Recruitment Checklist
description: A recruiter's sourcing pipeline checklist covering posting, sourcing, screening, ATS, and metrics.

items.text: Confirm the role requirements and ideal candidate profile
Agree on the timeline and target start date with the manager
Define the salary range and key selling points
Create the role and stages in your ATS
Decide which sourcing channels to use
items.note: Match channels to where this talent actually is.

items.text: Set target metrics for the pipeline
Draft a compelling, accurate job posting
Use inclusive language and clear requirements
Add a strong employer pitch and benefits
Publish to chosen job boards and the careers page
Share the role with employees for referrals
Track which channels each application comes from
items.note: Source data tells you where to invest next.

items.text: Search talent platforms for matching profiles
Reach out to promising passive candidates with personal messages
Tap referrals, alumni, and past silver-medalist candidates
Build a shortlist of sourced prospects in the ATS
Follow up with interested candidates promptly
Keep the top of the funnel full as roles progress
items.note: A dry pipeline stalls the whole search.

items.text: Review applications against the must-have criteria
Run consistent phone or video screens
Confirm experience, motivation, and salary expectations
Assess availability and notice period
Move qualified candidates to the next stage in the ATS
Send respectful, timely rejections to others
items.note: Every candidate is a potential future hire or referrer.

items.text: Keep every candidate's stage and status current
Log notes, scorecards, and communications consistently
Coordinate interview scheduling with managers and panels
Nudge stalled candidates so none go cold
Maintain compliant, complete candidate records
items.note: Data handling varies; follow local laws and privacy rules.

items.text: Keep hiring managers updated on pipeline status
Measure time to fill for each role
Track conversion rates between pipeline stages
Compare source of hire to find the best channels
Monitor candidate response and offer acceptance rates
Spot bottlenecks where candidates drop off
Adjust sourcing and process based on the data
items.note: Let metrics guide where you focus next.

faq.q: What does a recruitment pipeline include?
faq.a: It spans the job posting, sourcing, screening, interviews, and offers, with candidates tracked in an ATS at each stage. A healthy pipeline keeps enough qualified candidates moving toward a hire.
Through job boards, employee referrals, social platforms, talent communities, and direct outreach to passive candidates. A mix of channels keeps the top of the funnel full and diverse.

faq.q: What recruitment metrics should I track?
faq.a: Time to fill, source of hire, pipeline conversion rates, candidate response rates, and offer acceptance. These numbers reveal bottlenecks and show which channels deliver the best candidates.

faq.q: How is recruitment different from hiring?
faq.a: Recruitment is the recruiter's broad pipeline of sourcing and screening many candidates across roles. Hiring is a manager's end-to-end process for one specific role through to offer and onboarding.

faq.q: Can I print this recruitment checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, work through each pipeline stage, and check items off as candidates progress to keep your sourcing organized and measurable.
